builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LUDIUS: A Benchmark for Embodied Social Intelligence in Everyday Human-Robot Interactions
summary: LUDIUS replaces ad hoc or absent evaluation of vision-language-model social judgment in embodied agents with a structured benchmark of 15 social intelligence skills tested across simulated week-long household episodes, including a harness that feeds camera views, retrieves interaction history, and converts tool calls into robot actions. It costs nothing directly to the reader but adopting its methodology requires simulation environments, episode generation, and finetuning data that are not available under a constrained infrastructure budget. Its findings indicate that frontier models fail when reasoning about what a resident perceived earlier, reconciling competing interests, or acting under safety constraints and household norms, so any agent evaluated only on simpler tasks may overestimate its readiness for socially constrained deployment.
rationale: LUDIUS is an evaluation benchmark for embodied social intelligence rather than a deployable method, and its household-robot focus requires simulation infrastructure beyond the reader's production scope, though its evaluation-harness pattern is worth tracking for agent evaluation design.
technique: Benchmark for embodied social intelligence in VLMs
